snippets.snippet: payments-service is Sample Corp's core payments processing service, handling checkout authorization, capture, and refunds for all customer-facing storefronts. Tech lead: Priya Natarajan. On-call this week: Marcus Webb. Tier: Tier-0 (customer-impacting outage triggers immediate paging). Language/runtime: Go, deployed on GKE. Dependencies: checkout-service (upstream), ledger-service (downstream), Stripe (external processor). Related docs: the deploy and rollback runbook, and the PAY-2114 incident review. On-call escalation path: page the Engineering on-call rotation, then Priya Natarajan if unresolved after 30 minutes.

Deploying payments-service: 1) merge to main triggers the CI pipeline (lint, unit tests, integration tests against a staging ledger). 2) A canary rollout ships to 5% of pods for 15 minutes, watched against the canary-alarm dashboard (error rate, p99 latency, authorization failure rate). 3) If canary alarms stay green, promote to 100%; otherwise auto-rollback fires. Manual rollback: run `deploy rollback payments-service --to <previous-version>` from the deploy CLI, which reverts pods and drains in-flight requests gracefully. Marcus Webb is on call this week for any deploy that pages after hours; page via the Engineering on-call rotation for anyone else. See the PAY-2114 incident review for a real example of a canary-triggered rollback.

Severity levels: Sev1 (full outage or data loss, page immediately, open an incident channel), Sev2 (major degradation, page on-call, incident channel optional), Sev3 (minor/contained, file a ticket, no page). Every Sev1/Sev2 gets a written incident review within 3 business days (see PAY-2114 for a worked example) covering timeline, root cause, customer impact, and action items. The incident commander is whoever first acknowledges the page unless a more senior engineer explicitly takes over.

results.title: PAY-2114: Canary Alarms During Deploy — Incident Review

snippets.snippet: PAY-2114 summary: a payments-service deploy on 2026-06-28 tripped canary alarms 6 minutes into the 5% rollout — authorization failure rate rose from 0.2% to 4.1%. Auto-rollback triggered and fully reverted within 90 seconds; no customer-facing outage, but roughly 340 authorization attempts failed during the canary window and were not automatically retried. Root cause: a new connection-pool setting for the Stripe client was too aggressive for the canary pod's lower traffic share, causing premature connection eviction. Fix: the connection-pool floor now scales with traffic percentage rather than using a fixed value. Marcus Webb was on call and handled the response; Priya Natarajan led the follow-up fix. Action item: add a synthetic-traffic floor to canary pods so connection pools warm up correctly regardless of real traffic share — tracked as a follow-up ticket.

payments-service is a Go service backed by a Postgres primary/replica pair for authorization state and a Kafka topic (payments.events) that ledger-service and the fraud-review pipeline both consume. External calls go to Stripe for card processing. The service exposes a gRPC API to checkout-service and a REST API for internal tooling. Scaling: horizontally autoscaled on GKE based on request queue depth, with a floor of 6 pods to keep connection pools warm — the floor that PAY-2114's fix made traffic-share-aware for canary pods specifically.
